title: Conditional catch share accounted for 55% of the count-weighted thermal shift at 21 Finnish moth sites
abstract: We split the count-weighted thermal change at 21 Finnish moth sites between 1993-2002 and 2013-2022. For each resident species, mean annual relative catch share equals annual detection frequency times mean catch share when detected. An exact symmetric split assigned 0.137 C of the total 0.248 C shift to conditional catch share (55%; 95% spatial-block plus shared-year interval 25-70%). Resident annual detection frequency added 22%, recorded window entry 21%, and loss 2%. The two sequential product allocations gave conditional-share point fractions of 51-60%. Log-count weights reduced the fraction to 34%; equal survey counts gave 52% with an interval from -4% to 75%. Thus the result depends on weighting, and the data do not establish a majority contribution. This refines the earlier 77% resident term. It is not an independent monitoring replication. Catch share is compositional and combines abundance with capture. The split does not identify population growth, climate causation, or the cause of weak tracking in other taxa. Original code, aggregate results, source hashes and retrieval instructions are included.
